selected_script.angle: A damp melamine sponge crumbles on dirty bathroom grout and leaves gray residue instead of lifting embedded grime
selected_script.hook: I thought this sponge would erase the bathroom grout, but it just made a gray mess in the line.

timeline.0-3s: Extreme close-up of gray-brown embedded grime in a bathroom ceramic tile grout line near the sink; a damp melamine sponge scrubs back and forth but starts crumbling and leaves cloudy gray residue on the tile edges.
timeline.3-6s: Continue the same sponge method on the same grout line; the hand presses harder, the sponge pieces collect in the grout, the wet film spreads wider, and the grout still looks dark, showing effort and frustration without exaggeration.
timeline.6-10s: The Grout Cleaner Kit enters naturally beside the same stain: the white 32 oz Grout-eez bottle with red and blue label applies cleaner to the same grout line, then the bright blue V-shaped brush head with dense white twisted bristles scrubs along the line using an existing threaded pole; grime lifts realistically, the area is wiped clean, and the shot finishes on a credible side-by-side section of untreated dark grout versus cleaned lighter grout with a simple spoken CTA.

scenes.promptText:
Create one complete approximately 10-second vertical TikTok-style UGC cleaning ad in 9:16, realistic handheld phone-shot style, natural bathroom lighting, no polished studio look. Use the provided product reference images as the exact product identity: preserve the white 32 oz Grout-eez cleaner bottle, red and blue front label, Clean-eez logo position at the top of the label, ribbed white bottle neck, white cap, smooth plastic bottle body, glossy printed label, bright blue wide low V-shaped grout brush head, angled blue threaded socket, dense white twisted nylon bristles, material, proportions, color, shape, texture, and visible structure. Do not change product color, shape, material, size ratio, logo position, packaging, label layout, brush structure, or bristle look. Do not invent extra accessories, buttons, lights, interfaces, decorations, packaging, or exaggerated functions. The brush may be shown attached to a plain existing American standard threaded household pole for use, but do not present the pole as part of the kit.

Timeline: 0-3s: Start with an extreme close-up of a credible cleaning pain on a real bathroom ceramic or porcelain tile floor near the sink: a gray-brown dirty grout line with soap scum and embedded grime. A hand uses a damp white melamine sponge, a familiar ordinary cleaning method, scrubbing back and forth. The sponge visibly fails: it starts crumbling, leaves tiny white sponge bits and cloudy gray residue along the grout, while the grout line remains dark. Do not show the product yet. 3-6s: Continue the same failed method on the same exact grout line. The hand presses harder and scrubs faster; the camera stays close and shaky like a real phone video. The residue smears wider onto the tile edges, the sponge looks worn down, and the person shows mild frustration through hand movement only. Keep the stain believable, no extreme gross-out. 6-10s: The product enters naturally into the same shot: place the white Grout-eez bottle with red and blue label beside the dirty grout, apply a realistic small line of cleaner onto the same grout line, then use the bright blue V-shaped grout brush head with dense white bristles to scrub along the groove with steady pressure. Show real cleaning action: bristles agitate the line, damp grime loosens, then a simple wipe with a plain cloth reveals a visibly cleaner lighter grout section. Finish with credible proof in the same camera angle: a clear before-after contrast in one frame, with an untreated dark section on one side and the cleaned lighter grout section on the other. End with a light natural spoken CTA such as, “Check it out if your grout needs a reset.”

Important restrictions: no UI, no subtitles, no stickers, no text overlays, no captions, no watermarks, no floating graphics, no poster layout, no invented claims, no magical instant cleanup, no sparkling effects, no smoke, no fizz explosions, no exaggerated chemical reaction, no product drift, no perfect showroom transformation. Keep the result realistic for ceramic or porcelain tile grout and keep all action on the same stain area.
